# Source discovery report — 40% electronics import duty rumour

## Headline finding
The claim is not supported by any primary source. The earliest traceable
publication is tradejournal.example
(https://tradejournal.example/policy/electronics-duty-consultation-opens,
2026-06-28 16:40 UTC), which reports that a consultation on consumer
electronics duties has opened. It names no rate and no start date.

## How the claim drifted
The "40%" figure and the "next month" start date first appear together on an
aggregator post with no byline
(https://viral-roundup.example/2026/06/electronics-tariff), published after the
consultation notice and citing no document. The instruction to retailers to
halt orders appears nowhere outside that post.

## Corroboration of the underlying event
The consultation itself is confirmed independently by the ministry notice
carried at policywatch.example, published the same day, which sets a 60-day
comment window.

## Limitations
The aggregator post carries no timestamp, so its position in the chain is
inferred from the first archive capture rather than observed directly.
